findings.title: Discovery rejections and discovery harness errors are never saved as `SliceQualification` records
findings.description:
The first Functional Requirement says `build` "writes a `SliceQualification` for every slice index in it… Every rejected slice has a `SliceCandidateRejection` or `harness_error` with detail. None is silently dropped."

No task does this for discovery:
- Task 13's `discover` only returns `multiple_landings`, `branch_contains_merges` and discovery `harness_error` entries in a `DiscoveryResult`.
- Task 15 writes records only for candidates that `qualify_slice_candidate` sees.
- Task 20 (line 196) prints one line per index but never writes a record for a discovery rejection.

What breaks as a result:
- Task 22 (line 207) builds the yield rows from stored `SliceQualification`s, so `multiple_landings` and `branch_contains_merges` can never show a count. The design's Mitigation Strategies names exactly these two as the rules to relax if they dominate the yield rows.
- Task 22's test "every rejection value is listed when nonzero" cannot be met for those two values.
- Task 20's test "one line per index" checks printed lines, not records, so it would not catch the gap.

Fix: add a bullet to Task 20, or to Task 13, that writes a `rejected` (or `harness_error`) `SliceQualification` with `start_environment=None` for each discovery outcome. The bullet must also say which `landing_after_sha` goes into the record id when a slice has more than one landing, because D6's id requires a single landing. Task 20's test should then assert that a stored record exists for each index in the record. Task 13 should also say whether a discovery `harness_error` stops the build, as Task 20 says a qualification harness error does.

findings.title: Nothing brings 421–425 onto the slice branch after the precondition gate
findings.description:
Task 1 creates `426-slice.slice-cases` from the target while 421–425 are unimplemented (frontmatter `projectState`). Tasks 2–7 are committed on that branch. Task 8 (line 122) then greps `src/squadron` on the same branch and writes `BLOCKED:` if anything is missing. When 421–425 later land on the target, no step brings them onto the slice branch, so Task 8 will keep failing on resume unless the implementer improvises.

Conflicts are also likely on that refresh:
- Task 7 creates `src/squadron/benchmark/` and Task 6 creates `tests/benchmark/` before 421 creates them.
- Task 5 edits `config/keys.py`, which 421, 422 and 425 also edit (line 98 says so).

Fix: add a first bullet to Task 8: "merge the target into the slice branch. If it conflicts, abort, write `BLOCKED:` with the conflicting paths, and stop." The project's git rules allow a clean refresh from the target.

findings.title: Task 15 does not say how `slice_qualification_for` gets its lookup key from a case
findings.description:
`slice_qualification_for(store, case, environment)` must look up the record by (project, index, landing, fork digest). Task 25 calls it with a `BenchmarkCase`. According to Task 18 and D6, the landing sha on a case exists only inside the provenance string `source_ref = "slice:<index>@<landing_after_sha>"`. The task does not say where the index and landing come from. A junior implementer will most likely parse `source_ref`, which uses a provenance label as logical structure and goes against the project's rule on fragile labels.

Fix: name the source of each key field. One option is to look up by `case_id` (stored on `SliceQualification`) through `list_slice_qualifications`. Another is to add explicit fields if 421's `BenchmarkCase` already has them.

findings.title: Too many tasks for the work: qualification and judge-runner are split finer than needed, and two load tests trace to no requirement
findings.description:
The file has 42 tasks. Some of the splits add test files and tasks without adding coverage:
- **Tasks 15–19:** five tasks and five test files for the stages of one function, `qualify_slice_candidate`, all committed together at line 193. Merge them into two tasks with one test file each: pre-sandbox checks plus reuse, and the sandbox stages (sets, repeats, the case, harness errors).
- **Tasks 31–32** (lines 264–272): both build `plan_judge`. Merge them into one task.
- **Task 24's eight-concurrent-`invoke` test** (line 223) and **Task 33's 200-pair test** (line 276): the slice design states no NFR, and these trace to no success criterion. They also sit in `tests/benchmark/`, not `tests/load/`, and have no CI-gating task, so calling them load tests sets off that rule for no benefit.
  - In Task 33, keep the hung-dispatcher case (it covers the failure-mode rule) and drop the 200-pair scale.
  - Drop the concurrency test, or keep it as an ordinary test only if 424 actually runs `invoke` calls concurrently.

findings.title: Most success criteria have a task
findings.description:
| Criterion | Tasks |
|---|---|
| Case fields | 18 |
| Fixture rejections | 6, 13–15, 18 |
| P6 replay with cf in the scrubbed home, cf list unchanged | 24–26 |
| Grade and separate report tables | 36, 39, 41 |
| Normalization: synthetic tests and real fixture | 7 |
| Reference line not ranked | 37–38 |
| Over size, no truncation | 29, 34, 38 |
| Forfeits and harness-absent cases | 27, 30, 32 |
| Failure-path signals | 13, 19, 24, 31 |
| Refusals, bound, cap exit 2, resume | 31, 33–35 |
| Hand-computed pairwise tests | 37 |
| `tests/replay/` unchanged after extractions | 2–4 |
| Real-landing fixtures | 6 |
| Mixed-kind integration and yield rows | 22, 39 |
| Slash commands | 40 |

The only gap is the discovery-record issue above.

findings.title: Order, test-with pattern and commit markers
findings.description:
- The extractions and pure functions (Tasks 2–7) come before the gate.
- The cf spike (Task 10) comes before anything is built on cf, which matches D9's intent.
- Every implementation bullet is followed directly by its tests.
- `**Commit**:` markers are plain lines at tested points, roughly one per finished part of the slice. Live-run fix-up commits are conditional and skipped when no files changed.
- There are no circular dependencies.
- The design corrections in Task 1 are committed to the target as planning work before the branch is created.
